notes: Your old link, archived on the Wayback Machine (capture of 2 Aug 2017). BVA POP2017 'Intentions de vote vague 3, juin 2016', embargoed until 15 Jun. Its key-figures page gives ranges across hypotheses: Juppé 36, Le Pen 26-29, Hollande 13-15, consistent with your data. I did not open the per-hypothesis tables or see the fieldwork dates. The Commission's June 2016 list has no BVA notice.
Notice 8046 'Pres4 BVA PQR', fieldwork 9-11 Sep 2016, 8 hypotheses. In the notice your first scenario is hypothesis 2 (Juppé, without Bayrou): Juppé 36, Le Pen 30, Mélenchon 12.

Notice 8075 'Pres BVA pour la PQR'. Hypothesis 2 (Hollande, Juppé, without Bayrou): Juppé 37, Le Pen 29, Mélenchon 12.5, an exact match. But the notice gives fieldwork as 14-16 Oct 2016, not 14-19 Oct; 19 Oct may be the publication date.

Your old link, archived on the Wayback Machine (capture of 12 May 2013). CSA for BFMTV, 'Les Français et François Hollande', fieldwork 26-28 Apr 2013 online, 1,027 people (993 registered voters). Page 8: Sarkozy 34, Le Pen 23, Hollande 19, Mélenchon 12. This predates the 2016 law, so there is no Commission notice.

Your old La Libre link redirects here (article of 20 Feb 2017). The article text gives Le Pen 22.1 and Macron 21.3 with Bayrou standing, and Macron 23, Le Pen 22.6 without Bayrou, so both scenarios are covered. Fillon's share and the fieldwork dates are in the article's charts, which I could not read as text, so those two are not checked. There is no Commission notice (Dedicated Research is a Belgian pollster).

Notice 8169 'Pres Elabe les échos', fieldwork 30-31 Jan 2017. Both scenarios are on page 9. Hypothesis 1: Le Pen 26, Macron 22, Fillon 19. Hypothesis 2 (without Bayrou): Le Pen 27, Macron 23, Fillon 20.
Notice 8230 'Elabe L'Express', fieldwork 18-20 Feb 2017. Hypothesis 1: Le Pen 27, Fillon 20, Macron 17. Hypothesis 2 (without Bayrou) is also there.
Notice 8386 for BFMTV and L'Express, fieldwork 5 Apr 2017, 995 registered voters. Macron 23.5, Le Pen 23.5, Fillon 19, Mélenchon 17. The same notice is also listed as add/456.

Your old link, archived on the Wayback Machine. Future Thinking France / SSI press release dated 2 May 2013, fieldwork 26-29 Apr 2013 online. All 3 scenarios are covered. With Sarkozy: Sarkozy 32, Le Pen 22, Hollande 15, Mélenchon 15. With Fillon: Le Pen 29, Hollande 18, Fillon 16. A third scenario with Copé gives Le Pen 31.

This is the same file as your old harris-interactive.fr link, now hosted by Toluna (Harris Interactive's parent). For France Télévisions, fieldwork 6-8 Mar 2017 online: Macron 26, Le Pen 25, Fillon 20. The Commission notice is add/329, but the pages I looked at contained only the method and questionnaire.
Same file as your old harris-interactive.fr link, now on tolunacorporate.com. For LCP, fieldwork 5-6 Apr 2017: Macron 24, Le Pen 23, Fillon 19, Mélenchon 18. An identical copy is at …-LCP-1.pdf.

Notice 8018 'Pres ifop PM 21 juin', Ifop-Fiducial for iTélé, Paris Match and Sud Radio, barometer vague 3, fieldwork 14-17 Jun 2016. Published results, Juppé hypothesis: Juppé 35, Le Pen 29, Hollande 14. The notice contains at least 9 hypotheses (Sarkozy, Fillon, Le Maire, Macron, etc.). Your old ifop.com/media link is dead.
Notice 8120 'Pres IFOP PM', fieldwork 28-30 Nov 2016: Fillon 28, Le Pen 24, Macron 15, Mélenchon 11. The notice contains more than one hypothesis.

Notice 8236 'Rolling 16 Ifop PM', 'La présidentielle en temps réel #16', dated 22 Feb 2017: Le Pen 26.5, Macron 19.0, Fillon 19.0. As a rolling poll, its exact interview window was not legible in the text I extracted.
Notice 8260 'Roll 22 Ifop PM', rolling #22, dated 2 Mar 2017: Le Pen 26, Macron 24, Fillon 21.
Notice 8337 'Roll35 Ifop PM', fieldwork 18-21 Mar 2017: Le Pen 26, Macron 25.5, Fillon 17.5.

Notice 8364 'Roll 41 Ifop PM', rolling #41, dated 29 Mar 2017: Macron 26, Le Pen 25.5, Fillon 17.5. Rolling #40 (add/423, 28 Mar) has Macron 25.5, Le Pen 25, Fillon 17.5, so the two waves are easy to confuse.

Ipsos/CEVIPOF/Le Monde 'Enquête électorale française 2017', February 2016 wave, fieldwork 22-31 Jan 2016, 21,326 respondents. Three hypotheses are covered. With Sarkozy as LR candidate: Le Pen 26, Sarkozy 21, Hollande 20. With Juppé: Juppé 31, Le Pen 25. With Fillon: Le Pen 29, Fillon 19. It is linked from the Ipsos page 'enquete-electorale-francaise-vague-2-alain-juppe-en-position-de-force…' (9 Feb 2016). This predates the 2016 law, so there is no Commission notice.

Notice 8053 'Prims Ipsos Cévipof 26_09' (66 pages), for CEVIPOF and Le Monde, fieldwork 9-18 Sep 2016, 18,659 registered voters. The first-round chart gives the Sarkozy-hypothesis figures for Sept 2016: Le Pen 29, Sarkozy 22, Hollande 13. I did not count the other hypotheses (you have 4).

Ipsos for France Télévisions and Radio France, published 28 Mar 2017: Le Pen 25, Macron 24, Fillon 18, Mélenchon 14. The page links the full PDF (…/doc_associe/enquetepresidentielle1v4_1.pdf) and a technical notice giving fieldwork as 25-27 Mar 2017. Your old ipsos.fr link now redirects to the Ipsos home page. The Commission lists a matching notice (8357 'État d'esprit Ipsos France', add/417), but I could not open it.
Notice 8247 'Pres Kantar Le Fig', Kantar Sofres-OnePoint, fieldwork 23-24 Feb 2017. First-round chart on page 15: Le Pen 27, Macron 25, Fillon 20, Hamon 14.

Notice 8266 'Pres Kantar LCI', fieldwork 2-4 Mar 2017. Hypothesis 1 (Fillon), page 15: Le Pen 26, Macron 25, Fillon 17, an exact match. I did not view the second scenario's table (the notice also tests Juppé), so only the first scenario is checked.

Your old link is dead on odoxa.fr but archived on the Wayback Machine. Odoxa for Le Parisien/Aujourd'hui en France, 'Quels scénarios pour 2017 ?', fieldwork 29-30 Apr 2015 online, 1,021 people, published 5 May. Both scenarios are covered in the summary on page 5. With Hollande: Le Pen 29, Sarkozy 28, Hollande 17. With Valls: Sarkozy 26, Valls 20, Le Pen near 30.

Your old link, archived on the Wayback Machine. Odoxa for Le Parisien/Aujourd'hui en France, '2017 : l'hypothèse Juppé', fieldwork 21-22 May 2015, 911 registered voters. Both scenarios are covered in the summary on page 5. With Sarkozy: Le Pen 30, Sarkozy 25. With Juppé: Juppé 34, Le Pen 31. Hollande is given as '16 to 17%' across the two.

Your old link still works. Odoxa for Dentsu Consulting and Le Point, published 14 Apr 2017: Macron 24.5, Le Pen 23 (stated as 1.5 points behind), Mélenchon 19, Fillon 18.5. The full table is in an embedded slideshow. The Commission notice (8421, add/490) confirms fieldwork of 12-13 Apr 2017 but prints no results.

Your old link, archived on the Wayback Machine. OpinionWay for Le Figaro and LCI, 'Les Français et François Hollande un an après son élection', fieldwork 16-17 Apr 2013 online, 1,022 people (971 registered voters). Page 18: Sarkozy 28, Hollande 23, Le Pen 21, Mélenchon 11, Bayrou 11.

Your old link, archived on the Wayback Machine. OpinionWay PrésiTrack weekly summary for 13-17 Feb 2017, page 7: Le Pen 26 (on Friday), Macron 20, Fillon 20. The daily PrésiTrack notices for that week are also on the Commission site (e.g. add/266, add/262), but the results in them could not be read as text.

Your old link, archived on the Wayback Machine. PrésiTrack weekly summary for 17-21 Apr 2017, page 7: Macron 23, Le Pen 22, Fillon 21, Mélenchon 18, Hamon 8. The Commission notice for 21 Apr (PrésiTrack 55, add/528) exists, but I did not read its figures.

Notice 8383 'Pres Le terrain' (Scan Research / Le Terrain), fieldwork 23-27 Mar 2017. It matches the base of 586 people certain to vote and naming a candidate. But the notice (7 pages) has only the method, weighting and sample tables; I saw no voting-intention results in it. The old slideshare link has not been tested yet.

Your old link, archived on the Wayback Machine (it redirects to /publications/…). TNS Sofres/OnePoint for Le Figaro, LCI and RTL, fieldwork 14-15 Dec 2015 online, 1,000 registered voters. All 3 scenarios are on the page. With Sarkozy and Bayrou: Le Pen 26, Sarkozy 24, Hollande 19. Without Bayrou: Le Pen 27.5, Sarkozy 26, Hollande 22. With Juppé: Juppé 31, Le Pen 28, Hollande 20.
